text:
Marathon Petroleum jumped 3.8% today, recovering most of the ground it lost over the previous three trading days. The rebound follows a sharp drop from $475 to $457 as oil prices spiked to $116 on Middle East tensions, then fell back as Saudi Arabia's defense minister traveled to Iran for de-escalation talks. Today's move tracks the oil market's slight stabilization — crude still sits at $107.89 in the U.S., well above where it was weeks ago, and refineries are running at 93.4% capacity, which supports stronger margins for a refiner processing crude into fuel.

The stock's broader pattern over two weeks reflects the volatility in oil prices driven by geopolitical risk. Refiner profits depend partly on the difference between what crude costs and what they can sell refined products for — and when crude prices swing hard on war fears and peace hopes, that spread gets disrupted. The current run-rate of refineries and stable fuel inventories suggest the market isn't panicked about supply shortages right now, which helps the refining sector stabilize after the turmoil of the prior week.
